problem: Topological navigation is mostly teach-and-repeat, so planning graphs follow the recorded trajectory order and miss physical shortcuts between temporally distant but spatially close regions. Existing image-level or object-level loop closures give only sparse, geometry-free edges and weak control signals.
motivation: Loop closure in purely topological maps changes planning connectivity and cost propagation, unlike drift correction in metric SLAM, yet its downstream effect on navigation is little studied. Dense pixel-level relative-3D topologies (MASt3R-Nav) could turn loop closures into dense geometric shortcuts that give the controller fine-grained cost signals for any-point-to-any-point navigation.
key_idea: Detect revisited places with SeqVLAD retrieval plus UFM covisibility verification, and insert dense zero-cost pixel-correspondence edges between the loop image pairs in a pixel-level topological graph, so shortcuts reshape the WayPixel costmap that conditions the controller.
insight: Gains come from grounding loops in relative-3D pixel geometry, not from loop detection alone. Adding loops raises SPL-A from 28.65 to 62.43 for pixel-level, versus 13.41 to 27.61 for GNM-Adapted at image level. ObjectReact reaches similar SR (67.12 vs 68.49) but much lower SPL-A (46.82 vs 62.43). The detected loops (SeqVLAD+UFM) even beat GT-covisibility loops in SPL-A (62.43 vs 50.25), because covisibility filtering prunes pairs with small overlap and aliased structure.
method: Pixel topological map (from MASt3R-Nav): MASt3R gives dense correspondences and relative pointmaps within a temporal window. Matched pixels become nodes, inter-frame matches become zero-cost edges, and intra-frame edges cost 3D Euclidean distance, pruned to an EMST.
Loop candidate retrieval: SeqVLAD sequence descriptors over 5-frame windows, pairwise cosine similarity, threshold 0.4, temporal exclusion of ±3 frames.
Dense covisibility verification: UFM predicts per-pixel visibility (confidence > 0.9); the symmetric score is the min of the two directional visible fractions; a pair is kept if it exceeds 0.1.
Pixel-level loop closure: for each verified pair, MASt3R dense matches add many zero-cost inter-frame edges, stitching sub-trajectories and propagating shorter distances into the WayPixel costmaps.

Execution: the query image is matched to a local sub-map to give a pixel-level query costmap; a learned controller predicts BEV waypoints (position and yaw), refined by the CARE reactive collision avoidance and a history-based stuck-recovery rotation of 45°.

GT-covisibility loops (analysis): computed offline from GT depth and poses; a pair is a loop if more than 1000 3D points are consistent within 1 cm. Used as an oracle comparison and applied also to GNM and ObjectReact.

setting.backbone: MASt3R (matching and pointmaps) + UFM + SeqVLAD (pretrained, frozen) + learned WayPixel-costmap-conditioned controller from MASt3R-Nav + CARE
setting.training_data: Uses pretrained MASt3R, UFM and SeqVLAD and the MASt3R-Nav controller; the loop pipeline itself needs no new training and this paper adds no training data
setting.observation: monocular RGB, with depth and correspondences estimated by MASt3R
setting.action_space: predicted BEV waypoints (relative position and yaw) followed by a low-level controller
setting.privileged: none for the main method (the GT-Covisibility variant uses GT depth and poses as an oracle comparison)

numbers_note: Custom benchmark on self-collected HM3D trajectories, not a standard public benchmark. The MAE costmap table is not reproduced here.
results: On 73 HM3D start-to-goal episodes, PixelLoop reaches SR 68.49 and SPL-A 62.43, versus 35.62 and 28.65 without loops. It beats GNM+loops (27.40 SR) and GNM-Adapted+loops (32.88 SR), and beats ObjectReact+loops (67.12 SR, 46.82 SPL-A) mainly in SPL. On a real P3DX robot it gets SR 81.8 versus 36.4 without loops.
limitations: Evaluation is on a small self-collected set (73 episodes, 6 HM3D scenes, 11 real runs) and not a standard public benchmark.
Loop detection and graph preprocessing are offline and per-goal (~1 min per goal on a 350-frame map), and the map must be pre-built from a full expansive traversal.
Heavy compute: MASt3R inference takes ~173 ms and ~4.6 GB VRAM, giving ~4.8 Hz. Per-task and ablation analyses of loop-detection thresholds are limited.
